More: its menu picture

On the phone the tab bar is Today, Plan, +, Shop, More. More opens a drawer that slides up with Recipe Book, Kitchen, History, Prep, Reminders and Leftovers (agreed C-055). The 11-24 picture set (T-2147) has no More, so today it shows three plain beads. This page draws More in the same family: brown outline, flat colours from the Groceries bag, 2 to 4 bold parts, readable at 20 and 24 px.

The two finalists, side by side

Each in the phone tab bar: Today lit, then More lit; light, then dark. Then 20, 24, 48 and 128 in colour, the same in the plain cut (a greyed item), and on dark. Panel grades are from the final panel (Sonnet, Gemini), out of 10.

B, the pick: Chest of three, middle drawer slid out

A chest of drawers: the rest of the places are inside. Weak spot: it may read as storage or files.

The pick: round 8 B, Chest of three, middle drawer slid out
  • More opens a drawer, so the picture is a drawer: a narrow wood chest of three drawers (sage, sun, plum), the middle one slid out sideways past the right wall. The step in the outline and the dark gap left in its slot say “open” at 20 and 24 px, where round 5 did not.
  • Light in the tab bar: one ink frame at 1.1, drawer fronts as flat fills with wood between (no double borders), three short pulls, no feet. Three bold parts plus the frame, as light as Plan and Shop beside it.
  • Plain cut (a greyed item): one clean outline with the step built in, two lines between the drawers, the open drawer’s edge, three pulls. No masks at all in the 20 px cuts.
  • From 48 px up the open drawer shows its inside, with a bell top (Reminders) and a clock face (History) standing in it: several places, not one. Nothing rises above the slot or touches the drawer below.
  • Weak: a chest with an open drawer can also say “files” or “storage” (near Kitchen); the plain big cut is busy where the open drawer meets its slot. It changes the agreed ICON_STYLE line that calls More a plain mark (Tyler to OK). The alternative is the four tiles, round 3 fixed.
  • Round 8 (bug fixes from the final panel): wood strips stay between the drawers and the stroke is 1.2 at 20; the fronts are a half-step softer; the plain cut fills the empty slot instead of doubling an edge; the big cut’s open drawer is narrower than the chest and clear of the bottom drawer, with a whole bell and clock.

The pick, four ways

1 and 2 are for the tab bar and menus (20 grid); 3 and 4 for big places (48 grid). Plain cuts take the words’ colour (a greyed item).

Round 8

Round 8 fixes only the bugs the final panel found; no new ideas. Chest: a wider wood gap so the open drawer no longer covers the wood strips, strokes up to 1.2, fronts a half-step softer, the open front no wider than its slot; the plain cut fills the empty slot instead of doubling an edge; the big cut has the open front clear of the bottom drawer and narrower than the chest, with a whole bell (lip and clapper) and a whole clock. Tiles: the big cut’s clock is smaller and clear of the plum tile’s corner; the bell keeps its clapper in the plain cut.

Round 6

Rounds 6-7 answer the independent panel on round 5 C (Sonnet 7/7/6/7, Gemini 6/7/6/6): too heavy in the tab bar, the open drawer did not show at 20-24, the plain cut had a doubled box and a mask notch, and the big cut’s card punched the roof. Every cabinet now has one ink frame at 1.1, flat drawer fronts with wood between, no feet; the open drawer slides SIDEWAYS past the wall as a step in the outline; the plain cut is one clean outline (no masks); the big cut holds a bell top and a clock edge. A redoes the tiles with the round-3 fixes so the best tile can be set against the best cabinet.
